AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: This report describes an outbreak of gentamicin-resistant meticillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (GR MSSA) which occurred on a 21-bed neonatal unit (NNU) in Ninewells Hospital, Dundee, Scotland.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: An outbreak investigation was triggered by two new GR MSSA isolates from babies admitted directly to the unit who had acquired this organism during their stay. Data on MSSA cases and antibiograms of patient isolates were flagged as an alert and microbiology records trawled to detect previous cases.

AbstractText.Label: FINDINGS
AbstractText.content: Eight babies were affected by the outbreak strain over six months. Typing of all isolates by pulse field gel electrophoresis and spa typing showed that all were clonal complex 30, spa type t012. None of the outbreak strains were associated with bacteraemia apart from one baby who was born at a gestational age of 24 weeks and a birth weight of 500g. Observation of practice and environmental swabbing of an incubator suggested that this was the most likely source of spread of the outbreak strain. Three of eleven surfaces sampled were positive for the outbreak strain. On inspection it was found that the impeller was not routinely removed during cleaning and debris was seen in the housing. Swabs that were taken from the impeller and housing yielded the outbreak strain.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: GR MSSA isolates from NNU has been set up as an alert organism on the infection control system. No further cases were detected over a year's follow up after full compliance with the new guidelines for the cleaning and disinfecting of incubators were implemented.
